# PLAN — iteration 5
## Current state assessment
The verified incumbent is timing-feasible at 161 LUTs, 317 FFs, WNS 0.197 ns, and DSP 10. Iteration 2 missed setup timing; iterations 3 and 4 passed timing but used more LUTs (166 and 388), so neither improved the incumbent. The current seed stores all eight products and four partial sums as 28-bit values, although their exact ranges need fewer bits.

## Hypothesis
Using range-sized signed product and partial-sum registers, with explicit sign extension into the 28-bit accumulator, may reduce LUT and FF use while preserving the feasible timing and exact arithmetic.

## Instruction for generator
In `fir16_sym_core`, replace the eight 28-bit `product` registers with signed widths 20, 22, 22, 22, 24, 25, 26, and 26 bits, respectively; replace `sum01`, `sum23`, `sum45`, and `sum67` with signed widths 22, 23, 26, and 27 bits. Sign-extend each partial sum when forming the existing 28-bit `acc`, preserving exact signed arithmetic, rounding, saturation, and the existing stage enables. Keep the five-slot handshake, reset behavior, registered output, and top `// @latency 5` unchanged; compare routed LUT/FF and WNS/WHS against the incumbent.
